findings.statement: Demand for AI inference is growing faster than demand for AI training as enterprises move models into production.
Third-party analysts forecast double-digit annual growth for enterprise AI infrastructure.
Enterprise adoption of private or on-premises AI inference is rising, but many mid-size enterprises have not yet deployed it.
Export-control and licensing rules for advanced AI chips affect which regional cloud providers and countries NVIDIA can serve.
Data-residency and data-protection rules push regulated enterprises toward locally hosted inference.
Power availability and data-center build-out limit how fast enterprises and regional providers can deploy rack-scale AI systems.
The AI accelerator market is concentrated, with NVIDIA holding the largest share and a small number of rivals holding most of the rest.

metadata.source_note: These expected market, forecast, regulatory, and market-share claims are provisional hypotheses. Add dated independent sources and qualify the geography and timeframe before using them as a scored reference.
